pure-announcement.rationale: It is an ongoing protocol-design discussion among maintainers and implementers, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts (mcp-control-plane-layers, mcp-authorization-hardening) argue where enforcement should sit and how OAuth should be hardened; neither covers this thread's proxy-of-servers namespacing mechanics or the session/authority-boundary design constraints (immutable upstream routing tuples, per-tenant session isolation, hop-by-hop reverse-direction authorization).

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is a real, attributed GitHub discussion with linked PRs, issues, and a cited TSC meeting — independently checkable, not a bare claim.

durability.rationale: The thread is dominated by unresolved bikeshedding — the TSC's own consensus was that namespacing stays 'a documented best practice... not a mandatory protocol requirement,' and several sub-threads are explicit speculation ('hard to speculate at this stage') or client-specific regex bugs (Claude Code/Cursor) that will change independently of the protocol.

actionability.rationale: The closing comment gives a builder concrete constraints for a proxy-of-servers — keep an immutable upstream ID separate from the display name, scope sessions to the effective principal not just the upstream connection, treat reverse-direction requests as independently authorized hops, version the proxy manifest rather than mutating capabilities silently.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles several separable ideas — tool-name namespacing syntax, a Plan-9-inspired mounting proposal, client-specific character-limit bugs, and the session/authority-boundary principle — rather than one idea statable in a paragraph.
